description:
## What

Update AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5's `-cabf` unprincipled-exception clause to articulate the spec-taxonomy principle (decided 2026-05-13 in PKIX-jbvb discussion). Currently the clause uses "small curated reference set" / "small marquee-violation reference" language that's ambiguous about what counts as "small" once AI-grinding shifts the maintenance threshold.

## Decided principle

> `-cabf` crates ship idiomatic Rust Profile types for each subscriber-certificate profile/tier explicitly named in the underlying CA/B Forum Baseline Requirements. Variant subdivisions within a subscriber profile (e.g., EV vs non-EV TLS, EV vs non-EV code signing) are included. CA-cert and Root-cert profiles are NOT shipped as Profile types — those are path-validator concerns handled by RFC 5280 §6.1 logic. Per-predicate Lint enforcement is NOT shipped as Lints — that's `pkix-policy-zlint`'s job. The intent is operational: a caller writing `verify_smime_signer(..., &SmimeSponsorValidated, ...)` should get correct tier-aware enforcement without ever invoking zlint.

## Why the existing text needs updating

- "Small curated reference set" is ambiguous about whether it applies to (a) the BR taxonomy depth (how many tiers/variants of one BR), (b) the cross-spec horizontal expansion (no `-mozilla`, `-fedramp`, etc.), or (c) the per-predicate granularity. The principle says: (a) full BR taxonomy is in scope; (b) cross-spec horizontal stays barred; (c) per-predicate stays in `pkix-policy-zlint`.
- "Small marquee-violation reference" was framed around human authorship cost. With AI grinding transcription, the threshold is "what AI can grind faithfully with human review per BR refresh," not "what one human author can produce by hand."
- Without the amendment, future Mark / future agents drift back to either maximalist transcription (Lint-level predicates creep in) or minimalist transcription (subscriber-cert tiers stay incomplete).

## Specific text changes

In AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5, the **unprincipled exception** paragraph:

**Add** language clarifying the principle:
- Subscriber-cert taxonomy: in scope (Profile types per BR-named profile/tier)
- CA-cert / Root-cert path-validation: not in scope (RFC 5280 §6.1 handles)
- Per-predicate Lints: not in scope (pkix-policy-zlint comprehensive coverage)
- "NOT a template" stays for horizontal expansion (no `-mozilla`, `-fedramp`, `-dod`, `-etsi` admitted without explicit re-decision)
- Maintenance threshold revised to acknowledge AI-grinding

**Update** the "principled path for comprehensive CA/B Forum coverage is pkix-policy-zlint" sentence to distinguish *taxonomy coverage* (in `-cabf` scope) from *predicate coverage* (in zlint adapter scope).

## Acceptance

- [ ] AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 unprincipled-exception clause amended per above
- [ ] Memory `pkix-cabf-charter-2026-05-13` updated to reflect the revised principle (or superseded by a new memory keyed `pkix-cabf-spec-taxonomy-2026-05-13`)
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry in the workspace root (or rejection — AGENTS.md amendments may not be CHANGELOG-tracked depending on workspace convention)
- [ ] Commit message: `docs(AGENTS.md): articulate spec-taxonomy principle for -cabf crates`

## Cascade triggered after this lands

- PKIX-jbvb decomposed into .1/.2/.3 (3 S/MIME tier children)
- Potentially future beads for EV TLS / EV code signing / TimeStamping Profile types (deferred until user demand surfaces; principle is portable)

## Filed by

Filed 2026-05-13 during PKIX-jbvb discussion. Mark explicitly accepted the spec-taxonomy principle ("i like it, not pushing back"). This bead delivers the principle in AGENTS.md so future agents pick it up at session start.

## Cross-references

- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #5 (current text being amended)
- Memory `pkix-cabf-charter-2026-05-13` (PKIX-d5rh decisions; predates the spec-taxonomy clarification)
- PKIX-jbvb (S/MIME tier expansion; cascade child of this principle)
- PKIX-d5rh (CABF citation refresh; "no workspace-added rules" rule survives intact)
